data.name: Bushrahun
data.gender_notes: Bushrahun is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: She who conveys the good news, usually referring to a messenger or a bearer of good news. The name Bushrahun carries the meaning “Bringer of glad tidings” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Bushrahun usually hope their child will grow to embody bringer of glad tidings and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes hope and optimism, representing the light that illuminates the path and the good news that brings joy and happiness.
data.etymology: Bushrahun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bringer of glad tidings.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bushrahun total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bushrahun holds rich cultural significance, particularly within the Islamic tradition. The name Bushrah comes from the Arabic words 'al-busr' and 'ahhira', meaning good news or propitious news, which is a fundamental concept in Islamic and Arab culture. The name evokes images of messengers or prophets delivering important news, bringing comfort and reliance to the people they serve. Bushrahun is a beautiful tribute to the concept of the message-bearer, and has held deep resonance within Muslim communities over the centuries.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Bushrahun lies in its connection to the divine message and its messengers in the Islamic tradition. The name is a reminder of the importance of receiving and sharing good news with others, reflecting the concept of the Islamic virtues of mercy, compassion, and kindness. The name Bushrahun can also be seen as a reflection of the ultimate message of God's mercy and forgiveness, as conveyed through the Prophet Muhammad and other prophets throughout history. Ultimately, the name Bushrahun serves as a reminder of the power of message-bearers to bring hope and comfort to people, and the importance of spreading good news and positivity in the world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bushrahun: The radiant one with good news. In Islamic tradition, Bushrah was a wife of Prophet Luth (AS), carrying glad tidings of Allah's mercy and forgiveness. Her name signifies the triumph of faith over hardships, and the joyous arrival of Divine Grace.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hisham's Sirat Ibn Hisham, mentions Bushrah bint El-Fargham as the mother of Imam Ali Zain al-Abidin. She was a Christian slave-girl gifted to Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab (r. 634-644 AD) by his governor of Syria, Muadh ibn Jabal, when he was only 5 years old. When Umar grew up, he freed Bushrah and married her. They had a son, Ali Zain al-Abidin.
historical_references.context: Marriage of Caliph Umar to a Christian slave-girl and mother of Imam Ali Zain al-Abidin.

historical_references.reference: Al-Tabari's Tarikh al-Rusul wa al- Muluk, states that Bushrah bint El-Fargham was the mother of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba. She was a slave-girl owned by Marwan ibn Hakam, the Umayyad governor of Syria. When she was pregnant with Hasan, she was given to Caliph Ali (r. 656-661 AD) as a gift. He freed her and married her, and they had a son, Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba.
historical_references.context: Marriage of Caliph Ali to a slave-girl owned by the Umayyad governor of Syria and mother of Imam Hasan al-Mujtaba.
